description: New York motorcycle delta: helmet law and lane rules. National riding skills stay in core_motorcycle.json.

questions.q: Who must wear a helmet on a motorcycle in New York?
questions.explanation: New York has a universal helmet law. Every rider and passenger must wear a helmet.

questions.q: An adult passenger on a motorcycle in New York
questions.explanation: The New York helmet law covers passengers as well as the operator.

questions.q: Riding between lanes of moving traffic in New York is
questions.explanation: New York does not authorize lane splitting or lane filtering. Stay in a full lane.

questions.q: To ride a motorcycle on a public road in New York, you need
questions.explanation: New York requires a motorcycle license or endorsement on public roads. A car license alone does not cover the bike.

questions.q: A New York motorcycle learner-permit holder must ride under the supervision of
options: A licensed motorcyclist 21 or older within 1/4 mile
Any licensed car driver following in another vehicle
A parent or guardian riding along as the passenger
Nobody at all once the permit is 30 days old
questions.explanation: The supervising rider must hold a valid motorcycle license, be at least 21, and stay within one-quarter mile of the learner at all times.

questions.q: New York waives the motorcycle road test if a permit holder who has another class of license
options: Completes the Motorcycle Safety Foundation Basic RiderCourse
Logs 50 hours of supervised riding with a licensed rider
Holds the motorcycle learner permit for a full year
Passes the motorcycle written test a second time
questions.explanation: With another license class and a motorcycle learner permit, completing the MSF Basic RiderCourse waives the DMV road test.

questions.q: In New York City, a learner-permit holder may not ride or drive on
options: Any street within a city park
questions.explanation: Learner permit holders, including motorcycle permit holders, may not drive on any street within a New York City park.

questions.q: A New York motorcycle learner under 18 (Class MJ) must also follow
options: The junior driver restrictions for drivers under 18
No extra rules beyond those for an adult rider
Only the rule that every rider wears a helmet
The hours-of-service rules for commercial drivers
questions.explanation: An MJ permit or license carries the same graduated-license limits as a junior car license, such as the hours and the New York City limits.

questions.q: What does New York require for a motorcycle rider's eye protection?
options: Required unless the motorcycle has a windshield
questions.explanation: New York: eye protection is required for all riders.

questions.q: In New York, what is the youngest age for a motorcycle learner's permit?
questions.explanation: New York issues a motorcycle permit at 16 years at the earliest.
